new.title: Eat beyran and paça late at Sakıp Usta
new.desc: A family-run restaurant on Kemal Köker Caddesi in Alleben, founded about 54 years ago and now run by the founder's sons. It is known for beyran, paça (head and trotter soup), liver kebab and a triple künefe with ice cream. It keeps very long hours, which makes it a favourite for night-time beyran.
new.tip: Opening hours are reported differently (late night to 24 hours), so check before a very late visit.
new.q: Sakıp Usta Paça Beyran Kebap, Kemal Köker Caddesi, Alleben, Şahinbey, Gaziantep

new.title: Visit the Alaüddevle Mosque near Gaziantep Castle
new.desc: Alaüddevle Camii is one of the old mosques in the historic centre of Gaziantep, a short walk from the castle and the bazaars. The Medusa glass museum first proposed here is listed as permanently closed.
new.tip: Combine it with a walk through the nearby bazaar streets; dress modestly and avoid prayer times.

new.title: Explore ancient Sam'al at Zincirli Höyük
new.desc: Zincirli Höyük is the mound of Sam'al, an Iron Age city of about 40 hectares that became the centre of a Late Hittite kingdom. Akkadian, Luwian and Aramaic inscriptions were found here and some sculptures are now in the Louvre.
new.tip: A car is needed; combine with Yesemek and Tilmen nearby. Facilities are minimal.
